_meta.indication: KRAZATI is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with KRAS G12C-mutated locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), as determined by an FDA-approved test, who have received at least one prior systemic therapy.

pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 2 (Cohort A of a Phase 1/2 dose escalation and expansion trial)
pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, single-arm, multicenter, multicohort dose escalation and dose expansion trial
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with KRAS G12C mutated locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC; all 112 had received prior platinum-based chemotherapy and anti-PD-(L)1 based therapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary efficacy endpoint was overall response rate (ORR) by blinded independent central review (BICR), supported by duration of response (DOR)
pivotal_trials.n: 112 patients formed the primary efficacy population (Cohort A patients with measurable disease at baseline by BICR); Cohort A safety-evaluation enrollment was 116.
pivotal_trials.result: ORR by BICR 43% (95% CI: 34, 53); median DOR 8.5 months (95% CI: 6.2, 13.8), with 58% of patients experiencing a DOR of at least 6 months. The prespecified benchmark ORR of 23% was excluded by the lower CI limit.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%) included diarrhea (70%), nausea (69%), fatigue (59%), and vomiting (56%). Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 11% of patients. Severe GI reactions can occur; nausea, diarrhea, or vomiting occurred in 89% of 366 patients (9% Grade 3).
target_moa: Adagrasib is a small molecule covalent inhibitor of the RAS GTPase family that binds irreversibly to KRAS G12C, locking the protein in its inactive conformation.
companion_dx_detail: KRAS G12C mutation status determined by an FDA-approved test; the QIAGEN therascreen KRAS RGQ PCR Kit (tissue) is the FDA-approved companion diagnostic detecting the KRAS G12C mutation.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because it did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues in the intended population.

description.text: Added accelerated approval for Krazati (adagrasib) in combination with cetuximab for previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated locally advanced or metastatic colorectal cancer

citations.quote: This "Prior Approval" sNDA provides for the new indication of Krazati (adagrasib) in combination with cetuximab for the treatment of adult patients with KRAS G12C-mutated locally advanced or metastatic colorectal cancer who have been previously treated with fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin-, and irinotecan-based chemotherapy.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Overall response rate (ORR) supported by duration of response (DOR); the ORR and durable responses observed are reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit.

citations.quote: The ORR and durable responses observed with adagrasib are reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit and provide a meaningful advantage over available treatments for this
Primary endpoint of ORR with DOR is acceptable as a surrogate endpoint for accelerated approval.

confirmatory_requirement.text: Conduct a randomized comparative trial (PMR 4378-1), which may be met by the ongoing Phase 3 study of MRTX849 (adagrasib) versus docetaxel in previously treated KRAS G12C mutated NSCLC (KRYSTAL-12), to verify clinical benefit.

citations.quote: 4378-1 Conduct a randomized comparative clinical trial of adagrasib in adult patients with KRAS G12C mutated, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC who have received at least one prior systemic therapy, to obtain overall survival, progression free survival, overall response rate, and duration of response. This data may be obtained from the ongoing clinical trial entitled, "A Randomized Phase 3 Study of MRTX849 versus Docetaxel in Patients with Previously Treated Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer with KRAS G12C Mutation."

FDA also notes that 4 patients from Study 849-12 (KRystal-12; NCT04685135) are additionally included in the FDA pooled safety population for FDA's review of this application. KRystal-12 is an ongoing, randomized, multiregional clinical trial that is being conducted to verify the clinical benefit of adagrasib in patients with KRAS G12C-mutated NSCLC who have previously received platinum-based chemotherapy and an anti-PD-(L)1 antibody. Based on the original protocol, 340 patients will be randomized 2:1 to receive adagrasib 600 mg BID or docetaxel 75 mg/m2 until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. Patients on the docetaxel arm will crossover to receive adagrasib upon disease progression. The primary endpoint is PFS per BICR.
The clinical trials, KRYSTAL-1 and KRYSTAL-12 were performed using adagrasib in capsule formulation.

summary.text: Adagrasib (KRAZATI) received standard review and was granted accelerated approval according to 21 CFR 314.510 based on ORR supported by DOR from the single-arm KRYSTAL-1 Cohort A trial, with a required confirmatory randomized trial (Phase 3 vs docetaxel). It had Fast Track designation and orphan drug designation for KRAS G12C mutated NSCLC.
